q: Which of the following is a compulsory vaccine in the Expanded Programme on Immunization (EPI)?
e: Pneumococcal conjugate vaccine is given at 6, 10 and 14 weeks. Hib is also in the EPI, inside the pentavalent vaccine.

q: The following vaccines are live attenuated, EXCEPT:
e: The whole-cell pertussis vaccine is killed.

q: All are contraindications to vaccination EXCEPT:
e: Antibiotic treatment is not a contraindication to vaccination.

q: A woman positive for HBsAg delivers at term. The correct management of the newborn is:
o: Hepatitis B vaccine at 1 month only
Hepatitis B vaccine now and at 1 and 6 months only
HBIG only if cord blood is HBsAg positive
HBIG and hepatitis B vaccine within 12 hours, then complete the vaccine series
e: The newborn needs both passive (hepatitis B immunoglobulin) and active (vaccine) immunization at birth. Breastfeeding is allowed.

q: All of the following should not receive oral polio vaccine EXCEPT:
e: Children with asymptomatic HIV infection receive all EPI vaccines.

q: Which statement about vaccines is correct?
o: Live vaccines are advised in symptomatic immunodeficiency
After anaphylaxis to a vaccine, give the next dose
BCG leaves a scar that confirms vaccination
e: After BCG a papule becomes an ulcer and heals as a scar by 3 months. The varicella vaccine is live, and anaphylaxis to a previous dose is a contraindication.

q: Contraindications to vaccination include all of the following EXCEPT:
e: Antibiotics, mild illness, diarrhoea and admission to hospital are not contraindications to vaccination.

q: Which of the following is true about the conjugated Haemophilus influenzae type b (Hib) vaccine?
o: It is given only to high-risk children
It can be given from 2 months of age (6 weeks in the EPI)
It is contraindicated in egg allergy
It is not given after a reaction to DPT
It is a single dose without a series
e: Conjugation lets the vaccine work in infants. In the EPI it is part of the pentavalent vaccine, given at 6, 10 and 14 weeks.

q: Which of the following is a contraindication to measles vaccination?
e: The measles vaccine is live, so it is avoided in pregnancy. Malnourished children need it most.

q: Which of the following is an absolute contraindication to the pertussis vaccine?
o: Encephalopathy within 7 days of a previous dose
e: After encephalopathy following a previous dose, or with a progressive neurological disease, the other vaccine components are continued without pertussis.

q: In exams, which vaccine is linked to egg sensitivity?
e: The MMR vaccine is grown in chick embryo culture, which is the classic exam answer. In practice MMR is safe in egg allergy, while yellow fever and influenza vaccines need caution.

q: Which vaccine is contraindicated in an immunocompromised child?
e: Live vaccines (oral polio, BCG, measles, rotavirus) are avoided in immunocompromised children; inactivated polio vaccine is used instead.

q: A 4-month-old develops intussusception one week after a routine vaccine. The vaccine most associated is:
e: The rotavirus vaccine carries a very small risk of intussusception.

q: Which vaccine in the EPI is given intradermally?
e: BCG is given as 0.05 ml intradermally. The measles vaccine is given subcutaneously, and the pentavalent, pneumococcal conjugate and inactivated polio vaccines intramuscularly.

q: An infant has a painless left axillary node 2 months after BCG. He is well. The best management is:
e: Non-suppurative BCG lymphadenitis resolves by itself. A fluctuant node is aspirated.

q: A 6-week-old has mild diarrhoea and a temperature of 37.6 °C on vaccination day. You should:
o: Give vaccines after an antibiotic course
e: Mild illness and a low-grade fever are not contraindications; all the 6-week vaccines are given today.

q: A child missed the 10-week vaccines and comes at 6 months. The correct action is:
o: Continue the series from the missed dose
e: A vaccine series is never restarted; it is continued with intervals of 4 weeks.

q: Which vaccines are given at 9 months in the EPI?
e: At 9 months: the first dose of measles (MR) vaccine and meningococcal A vaccine (yellow fever vaccine in states at risk). The second MR dose is given at 18 months.
